The Ondo State chapter of the All Progressives Congress has said its reconciliation efforts are yielding positive results, dismissing reports of a leadership crisis and division within the party ahead of the 2027 general elections. The state APC Chairman, Babatunde Kolawole, said the party was working to unite all tendencies and strengthen its structure to secure victory for its candidates in the presidential, National Assembly and state assembly elections. Speaking with journalists in Akure, the state capital, on Friday, Kolawole said no member had been excluded from the reconciliation process, insisting that the party remained united. He said there was no reason for members to see one another as rivals, particularly as the state would not be holding a governorship election in 2027. “There is no rivalry, there is no division in our party. So, there is no cause for alarm. I can assure you we are on top of it and everything will be okay,” he said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources Also speaking, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign in Ondo State, Victor Olabimtan, said the reconciliation committee set up after the party’s congresses had reached out to party organs, interest groups and individual members across the country. He disclosed that the committee had visited Abuja to engage some party leaders and contacted others in Lagos and other parts of the country. Olabimtan added that he had personally reached out to some party leaders, while Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa had made the unification of all tendencies within the party a major responsibility since emerging as governor. He said, “Nobody is left out. All we need to do is to ensure that we put more effort into strengthening the existing unity that we are all enjoying in the party today. “So, there is no cause for alarm. As we make progress, you will also see that our efforts, the efforts of the governor, the party and its leaders are indeed yielding fruits to ensure that everybody is brought on board.” Olabimtan noted that President Bola Tinubu’s emergence had provided an opportunity for party members to put their differences aside and consolidate their unity. Similarly, the state Commissioner for Women Affairs, Seun Osamaye, pledged the support of women across the state for Tinubu’s re-election, saying a united front and collective mobilisation were crucial to achieving the one million votes target. “Ondo women are firmly behind the President and would work together to secure massive votes for him,” Osamaye declared.
